pr_title: Prevent data nodes from sending stack traces to coordinator when `error_trace=false`
pr_body:
This PR updates the behavior of data nodes to optimize error handling during search operations. When the query parameter `error_trace=false` is specified in the request (which defaults to `false`), data nodes will no longer send stack traces to the search coordinator node.

With `error_trace=false`, the stack trace is already excluded from the REST response to the client. By extending this to the communication between data nodes and the coordinator node, we further reduce unnecessary data transfer and lower the memory needed to handle search requests in case of errors in the coordinating node.

To implement this, the `error_trace` query parameter is passed to data nodes via the transport request header `error_trace`. This ensures consistent handling of the `error_trace` flag throughout the search request lifecycle.
After this change the `error_trace` header will be always sent to data nodes. Nodes with an older version will therefore have no way to specify if we want or not stack trace, therefore upon reading the header in the data node, if not specified we default to true, mimicking the current behaviour.

closes: #116772

issue_context.title: EsRejectedExecutionException instances consume an unreasonable amount of heap on coordinating nodes
issue_context.body:
Currently, if a data node rejects the execution of a query it sends a full `EsRejectedExecutionException` back to the coordinating node.
Each of these instances is then wrapped in a `ShardSearchFailure` and stored on heap on the coordinating node until all responses are received. Each instances practically comes out to about 50kb, resulting in searches targeting thousands of shards that all reject taking up hundreds of MB for these exceptions that will eventually not even see their stack-traces (which consume the bulk of the heap here) serialised on the REST layer.

Practically this leads to situations like this:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cea4da7a-c5c9-4582-9b08-8d09f7c74f0a)

A search targeting 5k shards that mostly sees rejections consumes over 100M for the exceptions until the response is serialised.
Outside of wasting heap, this can easily lead to a cascading failure effect in a cluster. Under sustained heavy load, once data nodes are overwhelmed as far as query processing goes, coordinating nodes can easily get overwhelmed by the heap consumption shown above.
The more shards targeted the easier it is to overwhelm a coordinating node but practically assuming constant rejections from the data nodes, there's currently a request rate above which any coordinating node gets overwhelmed.
